title: Full-read SSRF via ai.getModels / ai.testConnection - any authenticated user, no role check
summary:
# Full-read SSRF via `ai.getModels` / `ai.testConnection` - any authenticated user, no role check

## Summary

The AI-provider tRPC procedures `ai.getModels` and `ai.testConnection` are gated only by `protectedProcedure` (valid session; **no role or permission check** - every other procedure in the same router uses `adminProcedure`) and pass a fully user-controlled `apiUrl` into server-side HTTP requests with no URL validation, scheme allowlist, or private-IP filtering. Any authenticated user - including the lowest-privilege default `member` organization role - can make the Dokploy server send requests to arbitrary internal URLs and read the responses.

- `ai.getModels`: GET to `` `${apiUrl}/models` `` (or `/api/tags` when the URL contains `ollama`, `/models?key=` for `gemini`). On success the parsed model list is returned to the caller; on any non-2xx the **raw upstream body is reflected verbatim** in the error (`Failed to fetch models: <body>`) - full-read exfiltration of any content type.
- `ai.testConnection`: POST to `` `${apiUrl}/chat/completions` `` via the AI SDK (openai-compatible branch), upstream error text reflected in the error message.
- Full path control despite the fixed suffixes: a `#` fragment in `apiUrl` (`http://internal/secret#`) is stripped client-side by the URL parser, so the request line is exactly `GET /secret`.

## Affected

`Dokploy/dokploy` canary branch @ `c225188e` (2026-09-01). Confirmed live-exploitable on the published Docker image `dokploy/dokploy:canary` digest `sha256:269864cddc363f530b55d8607ace8ea89ad5a63de20ef1059f26ef6fdf0f6d8b` (built 2026-09-01); identical vulnerable code in `/app/.next/server/chunks/6355.js` of that image. Self-hosted default deployments (docker compose / install.sh), stock roles, no enterprise license. Pre-condition: any valid account - a freshly invited `member` suffices (standard collaboration flow). Class untouched by the 2026-07-21 advisory batch (all 60 published Dokploy advisories reviewed: command-injection / access-control / credential classes only; no CWE-918).

## Root cause

`apps/dokploy/server/api/routers/ai.ts:52` - `getModels: protectedProcedure` with input `z.object({ apiUrl: z.string().min(1), apiKey: z.string() })` (no URL validation), then:
- `ai.ts:61` (ollama branch) `fetch(\`${input.apiUrl}/api/tags\`, …)` / `ai.ts:127` (default branch) `fetch(\`${input.apiUrl}/models\`, { headers })` - sink; `ai.ts:131-133` reflects `await response.text()` in the thrown error for non-2xx.
- Provider/path chosen by substring matching in `getProviderName()` (`packages/server/src/utils/ai/select-ai-provider.ts:12-26`) - attacker steers the suffix via URL content (`":11434"`/`"ollama"` → `/api/tags`; default → `/models`).
- `ai.ts:286-318` - `testConnection: protectedProcedure` builds `selectAIProvider({ apiUrl: input.apiUrl, apiKey: input.apiKey })` and calls `generateText()`, which POSTs to `${apiUrl}/chat/completions`; AI SDK upstream error text is returned in the tRPC error message.
- `protectedProcedure` (`apps/dokploy/server/api/trpc.ts:161`) asserts only that a session exists - no `checkPermission`, no org-role gate. Sibling procedures in the same router (`one`/`create`/`update`/`getAll`/`delete`/`saveCustomProviders`) use `adminProcedure`, showing the intended privilege level.
- No SSRF guard exists anywhere on this path (no scheme allowlist, no DNS/private-range check, no redirect policy), unlike hardened fetch paths elsewhere in the codebase.

## Reproduction

Lab: `dokploy/dokploy:canary` (digest above) via docker compose, plus a benign in-network canary HTTP service serving sentinel strings (never contacted by the client directly).

1. Owner invites Bob with `role: "member"`; Bob accepts (`organization.inviteMember` → `/api/auth/organization/accept-invitation`), `member.role='member'`, no custom permissions.
2. Bob runs, with his session cookie:
